title: Before First Light
logline: A night-shift watchman fights sleep through the small hours, and when his attention finally sinks, his body slumps with it, and has to be caught and held up again.

object.note: Object 7 (identity not chosen) could enter only if a real moment on the night shift allows it. Never staged.

thread_in.thread: Kindness meets the body's fragility: from the tea trolley's night corridors to a tea factory's night shift, where a watchman's body sinks with his sleep and has to be held up again.

thread_out.thread: The long night's struggle to stay upright gives way to a harvest day kept steady by counting aloud, basket after basket, never losing the place.

requirements: A genuine night shift with a worker willing to be filmed over several nights
Employer permission that does not put the worker's job at risk
Enough low light to film without disturbing the work

suggestions.name: A tea or rubber estate factory running a night shift
suggestions.region: Central Highlands (e.g. Hatton/Dikoya or Nuwara Eliya district)
suggestions.why: Estate factories are well documented as running through the night during processing season.
suggestions.season_notes: Depends on the estate's processing calendar.
suggestions.verify: A specific estate, its night-shift practice and management permission are unverified.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Staying upright is not something a body does by itself. The texts describe a waking mind holding it up moment by moment, so when attention sinks into sleep, the body sinks with it.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ශරීරය කෙළින් තබා ගන්නේ අවදියෙන් සිටින සිත බවත්, සිත නින්දට බර වූ විට ශරීරයද ඒ සමඟම ඇද වැටෙන බවත් අභිධර්මය කියා දෙයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma names four origins of bodily matter: past action, mind, temperature and food. Matter born of mind is what moves the body and keeps it sitting or standing without falling; the faint mind that runs during deep sleep cannot do this, which is why a person who dozes off while seated or standing slumps. The texts also describe the body's lightness, softness and readiness for work as qualities that appear when food, weather and mind are suitable, and that give way to heaviness with lost sleep, fatigue, worry, heat or cold.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Across the small hours the camera watches the watchman's posture give way by degrees: the head drops and snaps back, a hand tightens on a torch or a rail, and tea and walking rounds become ways of pulling the body back up. At dawn the change in the body as the light comes is visible without comment, and the narration never names what the viewer has already seen.
lesson.caution: This is not 'mind over matter': the texts do not say willpower can cure a tired or ill body, only that a moment of mind is one of several things that move it and hold it up.
lesson.builds_on: The previous group found lightness and ease arriving with a kind mind; this film opens the body's stage by showing that the body's own uprightness and lightness also rest on the mind, and on sleep, food and weather, so kindness now meets a body that can simply give way.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
